resolutions.covered_by: src/sec10k/web/anchor.py (new, pure-stdlib mirror of index.html's algorithm) + evals/adversarial/ui-anchor-contract.json; index.html: coreOf/buildSourceIndex/findAnchor rewritten
resolutions.note: Both round-2 failure modes fixed, plus a third the fix's own full-fixture-set check caught before shipping. (a) whole-filing unanchored: root-caused to node-boundary whitespace being an arbitrary per-filing choice -- fixed by dropping whitespace from the matching problem entirely (coreOf/core_of strip it from both needle and haystack) rather than trying to model how much separator belongs at a join. This surfaced a THIRD bug: cat-2023's `Item 1.Business.` renders with ZERO characters between the nodes, which the round-3 draft (still inserting exactly one boundary space) also broke -- the core-strip design fixes both directions at once. (b) jpm-2024's confidently-wrong anchors: the `expectedFrac` fraction heuristic is REMOVED, replaced by body agreement -- among every occurrence of a heading, the one whose following core text shares the longest run with the item's own extracted `text` (its own heading prefix stripped first -- comparing item.text as-is scored 0 agreement at every occurrence, everywhere, a fourth bug the same full-fixture-set check caught) wins; below AGREEMENT_MIN agreeing characters (relaxed to the target's own length when shorter, so a genuine 5-char body like 'None.' still anchors), the result is unanchored rather than a guess. `find_anchor_frac` (the exact round-1 algorithm) is kept in anchor.py only to reproduce and pin the bug it caused.

v1_anchor_table.method: Live Browser tool run against all 37 real fixtures (aapl-2026-10q and ksb-2007 are non-10-K/unsupported and truncated-download extracts zero items, so all three show 0/0/0 correctly). For each item with a heading_text, scrollSourceToItem() was called and the RESULT WAS VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY of findAnchor's own scoring, via document.caretRangeFromPoint() reading the actually-rendered DOM text near the top of the source pane after scrolling, compared against the item's own heading/body core. 'wrong' = anchored but the rendered text at the anchor does not agree with the item.

per_fixture.note: Item 6 'Reserved': heading repeats (TOC + body) and the body is EMPTY ('Item 6. Reserved' with nothing after it) -- no signal exists to disambiguate, so find_anchor correctly reports unanchored rather than guessing (hard rule 4). Items 1, 1A, 1B, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 7A, 8, 9, 9A -- every item round 2 shipped wrong on this fixture -- now all anchor correctly and were independently verified.

This fixture is deliberately malformed markup. Python's html.parser (used by anchor.py's visible_text_chunks, which cross-checks the ui-anchor-contract eval case) and the browser's own much more lenient, error-correcting HTML parser structure this specific malformed document differently, so the DOM text-node layout the live browser sees for item 8 diverges from what anchor.py sees -- an honest miss in the browser, not a wrong anchor, and a disclosed limitation of using a stdlib parser as a DOM proxy rather than a defect in the algorithm itself.

python_mirror_cross_check.note: evals/adversarial/ui-anchor-contract.json runs the same algorithm in Python (src/sec10k/web/anchor.py) across the same 38 fixture dirs / 641 items, gated in the invariant/fast suites. 0 failures, with jpm-2024 Item 6 excluded as an honest miss by the same reasoning as the browser run. Confirms the live browser numbers are not a one-off measurement -- the algorithm's contract is pinned and will go red on a future regression even without a browser.
